claims.claim: At a pension in Florence, Lucy Honeychurch and her cousin and chaperone Miss Bartlett complain
claims.evidence: Ch. I 'The Bertolini'; 'the chaperon of my young cousin, Lucy'

claims.claim: They were promised south rooms with a view but given north rooms facing a courtyard
claims.evidence: 'south rooms with a view... north rooms, looking into a courtyard'

claims.claim: Mr. Emerson and his son George offer to swap rooms
claims.evidence: 'you can have our rooms, and we'll have yours'; George: 'It's so obvious they should have the rooms'

claims.claim: Lucy visits Florence with her cousin Charlotte Bartlett and meets the Emersons
George kisses her in a field of violets
claims.evidence: 'a little open terrace, which was covered with violets... He stepped quickly forward and kissed her.'
Miss Bartlett calls 'Lucy!'; Ch. VII 'They Return' (Charlotte parts them)

claims.claim: In Surrey, Lucy becomes engaged to the fastidious Cecil Vyse
claims.evidence: 'after the engagement was announced'; Cecil like 'those fastidious saints'; Summer Street / Windy Corner

claims.claim: The Emersons rent Cissie Villa nearby, George declares his love again
claims.evidence: Freddy: 'Emerson'; 'the tenants moved into Cissie Villa'; George's later approach

claims.claim: Lucy breaks with Cecil but denies her feelings
claims.evidence: 'I broke off my engagement because I did not love George'

claims.claim: She plans to go to Greece (with the Miss Alans)
claims.evidence: 'I would give anything to go with them'; 'I must go to Greece because I do not love George'

claims.claim: Old Mr. Emerson tells her she loves George
She marries George; novel ends in Florence where they guess Miss Bartlett secretly hoped
claims.evidence: 'Siamo sposati'; 'we return to the Pension Bertolini'; George: 'she hoped, far down in her mind'

claims.claim: Lucy: young Englishwoman between Cecil and George
George: moody, honest young man who loves Lucy

claims.evidence: 'This is my son... his name's George'

claims.claim: Charlotte Bartlett: Lucy's fussy older cousin and chaperone

claims.evidence: 'the boy, who was Freddy, Lucy's brother' found; 'younger' and 'cheerful' not established
